passages.note: Umberg voted Aye on Senate final passage (29-8, about 20% No, so not near-unanimous) of the Senate-amended text that was chaptered.
passages.actor_quote: Rubio, Skinner, Smallwood-Cuevas, Umberg, Wahab, Wiener

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Operative Sec. 220.5 forbids local rules requiring disclosure (rung 2); it does not require staff to withhold (excludes rung 1) and bars disclosure-on-request or notification mandates (excludes rungs 3-5); the bill is single-subject (LGBTQ pupil rights).

rows.reasoning: Umberg voted Aye on Senate final passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), whose operative Section 220.5 says schools and boards "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose" a pupil's gender identity without consent. That is the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill only says staff shall not be required to disclose, so it does not reach "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents".
